data.gender_notes: Brisa is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Spanish word 'brisa', meaning breeze or gentle wind. The name is often given to girls born on windy days or those who embody the refreshing qualities of a gentle breeze. The name Brisa carries the meaning “Breeze or gentle wind” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Brisa usually hope their child will grow to embody breeze or gentle wind and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes the gentle touch of God's grace and the refreshing peace it brings.
data.etymology: Brisa belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Breeze or gentle wind.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Brisa total 4, giving a life-path number of 4. Number 4 is linked with Rahu and with the qualities of stability, discipline and hard work.

in_hebrew.name: בריסה
in_hebrew.meaning: ברכה רוחנית נשימה של אלוהים ברוח הקודש
in_hebrew.long_meaning: השם בריסה נגזר מהמילה העברית 'ברכה' שפירושה ברכה או מתנה מאלוהים, ו-'רוח' שפירושה רוח או נשימה. ביחד, השם בריסה מייצג את נשימת האלוהים ברוח הקודש, מבטא את הרעיון של ברכה רוחנית ומתנה מאלוהים.

in_greek.name: Βρίσα
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Βρίσα συνδέεται ετυμολογικά με τη λέξη 'πνοή' που σημαίνει πνοή ή αναπνοή. Στο πλαίσιο της χριστιανικής παράδοσης, το όνομα Βρίσα μπορεί να ερμηνευτεί ως η θεία πρόνοια ή η πνοή του Θεού, αντανακλώντας την πνευματική και θεϊκή σχέση.

in_latin.name: Brisa
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen Brisa derivatur ex voce Latina 'flatus' seu 'spiritus', quae respirationem vel ventum significat. In traditione christiana, nomen Brisa connotare potest flatum divinum seu spiritum Dei, exprimens ideam inspirationis caelestis et doni spiritualis.

historical_references.reference: Brisa of Portugal, also known as Brisarella or Brisas de Avis, was a Portuguese noblewoman and queen consort of Castile. She was the daughter of Peter, Duke of Coimbra, and granddaughter of King John I of Portugal. Brisa married King Alfonso XI of Castile in 1325, when she was around eleven years old. After Alfonso's death in 1350, Brisa became regent for her son Henry of Trastamara, who was only three years old at the time. Brisa ruled as regent until her son's majority in 1366, during which time she successfully defended the kingdom against rebellion and foreign invasion.

Brisa of Rimini, also known as Brisarella, was an Italian noblewoman and a central figure in the conflict between the Guelph and Ghibelline factions in the 13th century. She was the wife of Guido da Montefeltro, the lord of Rimini, and the mother of Federico da Montefeltro, who became the condottiere of the papal army. Brisa is best known for her role in the Battle of Montaperti (1260), where she is said to have disguised herself as a man and fought alongside her husband's army. Her intervention is credited with turning the tide of the battle in favor of the Guelphs.
